title: Prime Big Deal Days' Early Deals Are Already Live — Here's What's Actually Worth Buying Before the Official October 6 Start
intro: Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days doesn't officially open until 12:01 a.m. PDT on October 6, but deal-tracking sites have been posting real, live "early access" listings for days already — new ones have shown up on Slickdeals as recently as today. Most of the early wave skews toward cameras, mesh routers, and TVs, but a handful of apartment-gardening-relevant items are already marked down for real, which matters right now specifically because early October is seed-starting season for anyone planning a windowsill herb garden through the dark months. Three items are worth calling out by name, with the actual prices that are live today — and one honest caveat about which of these "deals" are genuine markdowns versus a recurring price point these items hit every few months regardless of any sale banner.

sections.heading: A self-watering seed starter kit, for the herb seeds you'd otherwise start too late
sections.body: Burpee's 72-Cell Self-Watering Seed Starter Tray Kit — two 36-cell trays, a self-watering mat and reservoir tray, 72 coir growing pellets, and a humidity dome — is listed for Prime members at $11.88 with free shipping as of today's early-deals wave. That's squarely in the window where it's useful: basil, parsley, and chives started indoors now have roughly 8-10 weeks to get established before the shortest-daylight stretch of the year makes new seedlings struggle, and a self-watering mat removes the single most common seed-starting failure, which is drying out a tray during a workday instead of babysitting it with a spray bottle.

products.name: Burpee 72-Cell Self-Watering Seed Starter Tray Kit
products.blurb: A self-watering mat and reservoir tray under the actual seed cells, which is the difference between a tray that survives a missed watering day and one that doesn't — useful for starting indoor herb seeds now, well ahead of the lowest-light weeks of the year.
products.priceNote: Listed at $11.88 for Prime members in today's early Prime Big Deal Days wave; check current Amazon pricing.

sections.heading: A self-watering raised planter, if your 'indoor herb garden' is actually a balcony rail
sections.body: Keter's Urban Bloomer is a resin raised garden bed with a built-in water-level gauge and a drainage plug, sized at 12.7 gallons — the dark grey version is currently listed at $60.46 for Prime members, against a list price that runs well over $100 for comparable Urban Bloomer sizes at other retailers. For apartment balconies that are too small for a full raised bed but too exposed for loose pots, a self-watering reservoir means the gap between watering trips (a real problem once cold weather makes balcony checks less frequent) stretches from a day or two to closer to a week.

products.name: Keter Urban Bloomer 12.7-Gallon Self-Watering Raised Garden Bed
products.blurb: A resin raised planter with a water-level gauge and drainage plug built in, sized for a balcony rather than a yard — the self-watering reservoir is the actual point, since it buys several extra days between watering trips as the weather turns and balcony checks get less frequent.
products.priceNote: Listed at $60.46 for Prime members in today's early deals, against a list price over $100 for comparable sizes at other retailers; check current Amazon pricing.

sections.heading: The one 'deal' worth checking a price tracker on before buying
sections.body: Budget 84-LED clip-on full-spectrum grow lights with dimmable levels and a built-in timer have shown up repeatedly on deal-tracking sites over the past year at prices between $9 and $13 — this is a recurring price floor for this exact category of light, not a one-time Prime Big Deal Days markdown, and the same listing has carried a near-identical "deal" tag multiple times since 2025. That doesn't make it a bad light for a single seed tray or a small herb pot; it means the honest move is to check the listing's price history on a free tool like CamelCamelCamel before treating the Prime Big Deal Days banner as the reason to buy, since this specific category tends to sit at that price most of the year anyway.

products.name: 84-LED full-spectrum clip-on grow light with timer
products.blurb: A small clip-mounted grow light with dimmable brightness and a built-in timer, enough for a single seed tray or small pot — worth owning at its usual $9-13 price point, just worth confirming on a price-history tool that today's listing is actually that price and not a markup dressed up as a Prime Big Deal Days discount.
products.priceNote: Has repeatedly listed between $9 and $13 over the past year on deal-tracking sites; this is this category's normal price floor, not necessarily a Prime-specific markdown — check price history before buying.

conclusion: The official Prime Big Deal Days event starts October 6, but real early listings are already live today, and for apartment growers the two genuinely worth acting on are the self-watering seed starter kit and the self-watering raised planter — both tied to a real seasonal need (starting herb seeds now, stretching balcony watering intervals as the weather turns) and both priced meaningfully below their usual range. The clip-on grow light is fine to buy if you need one, but treat its "deal" tag with more skepticism than the other two — it's a category that sits near this price most of the year.
